newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela sets 60 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela sets 60 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.

text.p: The Central Bank of Venezuela announced for Wednesday morning a 40 billion bolivar ($83 million) auction of 178-day "monetary stabilization," or TEM, bills with a 18.70 percent coupon.
The bank said it would also offer 15 billion bolivars ($31 million) in 266-day bills with a 19.13 percent coupon, and another 15 billion bolivars of 358-day bills with a 19.58 percent coupon.
Some 26 billion bolivars of TEMs are due to mature on Thursday.

Coupons at the Wednesday auction are up from last week's 60 billion bolivar issue. Then 178-, 267- and 351-day notes carried 16.89, 17.24, and 17.58 percent coupons respectively for effective yields that rose as much as 243 basis points to 18.71, 20.61 and 21.89 percent.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
